title: Apotheosis-Artifice
description: Apotheosis Artifice is an addon for the Apotheosis mod that adds new ways to reforge, store, and manipulate equipment through the Curios slot system.
body:
Apotheosis Artifice is an addon for the Apotheosis mod that adds new ways to reforge, store, and manipulate equipment through the Curios slot system.

## Features

### Curios Reforging
- Apply Apotheosis reforge operations to any item equipped in a Curios slot, including charms, rings, belts, and curios-specific equipment.
- The reforge selection interface now supports multiple slot targets in a single action.

### Multi-Slot Reforge Selection
- Browse and select reforge targets across all equipped Curios slots from a unified menu.
- Apply a reforge to one or many slots without reopening the inventory.

### Gem Storage Cases
- New Curios items that act as portable gem pouches.
- Store, sort, and retrieve Apotheosis gems directly from the equipped case, without opening a chest.
- Composite item model renders as a single in-world icon regardless of stored contents.

### Precision Enchanting Table
- A new block variant focused on fine-grained control over Apotheosis enchanting workflows.
- Surfaces every relevant stat that influences the outcome, so you can predict the result before committing.

### Portable Salvaging Tool
- A Curios item that performs Apotheosis salvaging on demand, anywhere.
- Useful for breaking down unwanted gear without returning to a dedicated block.

## Why use it

If you already play Apotheosis and Curios, this mod connects the two systems so reforging, gem storage, enchanting, and salvaging all work through your equipped slots instead of requiring dedicated blocks or chests.

## Required dependencies

- Apotheosis 7.4.x
- Curios 5.2.x or newer (5.x line)
- Placebo 8.6.x
- Forge 47.x for Minecraft 1.20.1

## Notes

- This mod is an addon and does nothing useful without Apotheosis installed.
- Game-test suite runs under the namespace `apotheosis_artifice`.
- Source: derived from Apotheosis by Shadows_of_Fire (Stormraven Studios, LLC), used under MIT.
